method_card.title: Powers, Roots and Standard Form
steps: A power is repeated multiplying; a root undoes it. Learn the squares to 15² and cubes to 5³.
Standard form is A × 10 to the n, with A between 1 and 10; the power counts the decimal places moved.
Multiply: multiply fronts, add powers. Divide: divide fronts, subtract powers.
Always adjust the front back between 1 and 10 and change the power to match.
method_card.content:
Powers are repeated multiplying: \(a^n\) is \(n\) copies of \(a\). Roots reverse them, so \(\sqrt{}\) undoes squaring and \(\sqrt[3]{}\) undoes cubing. A negative index means one over the positive power.

Standard form writes a number as \(A \times 10^n\) with \(1 \le A < 10\). Big numbers take a positive \(n\), numbers below 1 take a negative \(n\). To multiply, multiply the fronts and add the powers; to divide, divide the fronts and subtract the powers, then adjust \(A\) back below 10.
method_card.example:
Write 0.00045 in standard form.

Move the point after the first non-zero digit to get \(4.5\); it moved 4 places right, and the number is below 1, so \(n = -4\).

Answer: \(4.5 \times 10^{-4}\)

bronze.title: Bronze: Powers, roots and writing standard form
steps: A power is repeated multiplying: \(5^3 = 5 \times 5 \times 5\). A square root undoes squaring, a cube root undoes cubing.
Standard form is \(A \times 10^n\) with A between 1 and 10. Move the point to sit after the first digit and count the places.
Big numbers (above 1) get a positive power; small numbers (below 1) get a negative power.

silver.title: Silver: Multiplying and dividing in standard form
steps: Multiply: multiply the fronts and add the powers. Divide: divide the fronts and subtract the powers.
Then adjust: if the front reaches 10 or more, move it below 10 and add 1 to the power.
A negative index means one over the positive power: \(4^{-2} = \frac{1}{4^2} = \frac{1}{16}\).

gold.title: Gold: Adjusting, adding and real contexts
steps: After multiplying or dividing, always adjust the front back between 1 and 10. A front below 1 (like 0.8) means take 1 off the power.
To add or subtract, the powers must match. If they differ, write both as ordinary numbers, combine, then rewrite in standard form.
In word problems, pick the operation first (distance is speed × time), then work the fronts and powers.

opener.label: Before any powers
opener.display:
The Moon is about 384,000 km away. Writing all those zeros is slow and easy to slip on, so scientists pack them into a power of 10.
The highlighted part is the three trailing zeros.

steps.pre: How many zeros are on the end of 384,000?
Each zero is one ×10. Three zeros multiplied is 10 to the power of what?

steps.say: Those three zeros are exactly \(10^3\), so \(384{,}000 = 384 \times 10^3\). Tidy the front to a single digit and it becomes \(3.84 \times 10^5\). That is standard form: one digit before the point, times a power of 10, where the power counts how far the point moved. Big numbers get positive powers, tiny numbers get negative ones.
Standard form is \(A \times 10^n\) with A between 1 and 10. Find A first.
